title: Emergency Childbirth
summary: Call for help and follow the dispatcher's instructions. Birth is usually natural: support the baby, keep mother and baby warm, and never pull on the baby or cord.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} – the dispatcher will talk you through the birth
when: Labour has started and birth is imminent (urge to push, baby's head visible)
Heavy bleeding, cord comes out first, baby's bottom or feet come first
Baby is not breathing or crying after birth

steps.title: Call {EMERGENCY} and prepare
steps.text: Put the phone on speaker. Wash your hands and wear gloves. Get clean towels, blankets and a warm place. Help the mother into a comfortable position – usually half-sitting, knees bent.

steps.title: As the baby is born
steps.text: Let the birth happen naturally. As the head appears, support it gently – do not pull. The shoulders and body usually follow quickly with the next contraction. Support the baby as it is born.
steps.caution: Never pull on the baby's head, body or the umbilical cord.

steps.title: Dry and warm the baby
steps.text: Dry the baby with a towel and place it skin-to-skin on the mother's chest. Cover both, including the baby's head. Wipe fluid from the baby's mouth and nose.
points: If the baby is not breathing or crying, rub its back firmly. If still not breathing normally, start infant CPR

steps.title: Umbilical cord and placenta
steps.text: Do not cut or pull the cord – leave it for the responders. The placenta usually delivers within 30 minutes; let it come naturally and keep it with the baby.

steps.title: Care for the mother
steps.text: Keep her warm and comfortable. Watch for heavy bleeding. Gently rubbing the lower abdomen and breastfeeding can help the womb contract.

warningSigns: Baby not breathing, blue or floppy
doNot: Do not pull on the baby or the cord
Do not try to delay the birth
Do not cut the cord unless the dispatcher tells you to
Do not let the baby get cold
